decisions.reason: At epsilon_Psi=0 the asserted strict inequality is 0<0, which is false. Require epsilon_Psi>0 for the OP5 specialization, preserving its strict error guarantee. The prefix induction gives sqrt(w_tau/(T/2)); complemented leaf labels preserve these amplitudes by sine reflection. Unitary telescoping gives (T-1)epsilon_Psi/(100T)<epsilon_Psi/100, also for the inverse. No choice axiom is used.

Step 2 allocated simulation tolerances without executing the controlled evolutions, so the literal procedure had no H-dependent phase. Added each forward call controlled on q_j: with this carrier’s explicitly declared order q_(L-1)...q_0, tau=sum_j 2^j x_j, yielding exp(+i H tau t0/T). The digest’s suggested q_(L-1-j) would reverse significance under this carrier’s wire names. Actual circuit adjoints remain the reverse calls. Extended the rational accuracy input to 0<p_epsilon<=q_epsilon; kernel, perturbation, normalization and 4epsilon/(4096 kappa) implementation bounds all cover epsilon=1. Also corrected the prefix-mass formula citation to its actual supplier lemma.

Zero eigenvalues are admissible off the input support, so summing beta_j/lambda_j over the full basis contains undefined 0/0 terms. Restricted only the reciprocal and probability sums to J={j:beta_j!=0}; on J the support promise gives 1/kappa<=|lambda_j|<=1 and the squared coefficients still sum to one. The Penrose construction in step 1.1 already defines the pseudoinverse correctly on the kernel. The convex-average probability bounds and normalized target are unchanged; this is a nonfatal explicit-support notation repair.

The rejection overlooks both this item’s F1, which explicitly gives K calls of each type per round, and the cited capped-amplification proof step 3.1. An accepted draw j<K uses j+1<=K calls to V and j<=K-1 calls to V-adjoint; a rejected draw uses none. Summing R rounds proves the separate RK caps. K<=5kappa and R<=16ln(1/rho)+17 give the asserted order; each V contains one B and each inverse one B-adjoint. No item edit is needed.

At kappa=1 both eigenvalues coincide, so the title incorrectly promises two distinct eigenvalues throughout the stated domain. Retitled to Two-dimensional diagonal HHL inversion, retaining kappa>=1. Direct inversion gives (|0>+kappa|1>)/sqrt(1+kappa^2); its ideal probability (1+kappa^2)/(8kappa^2) lies in (1/8,1/4], including p=1/4 at kappa=1. The grid spacing is pi epsilon/(1024kappa), with no hard tail cutoff asserted. Example and verification content remain unchanged.

The theorem advertises epsilon=1 while its supplying algorithm originally excluded that rational input. This nonfatal interface inconsistency is repaired in the assigned supplier by permitting p_epsilon=q_epsilon; the theorem carrier needs no change. The kernel supplier and perturbation proof cover 0<epsilon<=1. Their relative kernel error is at most 10sqrt(300)epsilon/2048; the four implementation budgets add at most epsilon/512 relative error. Their sum is below 0.09epsilon, giving norm(u)>1/(4kappa), the amplification lower bound and normalized distance <epsilon also at epsilon=1. The domain-tag projection fixes the ideal dilation target and contracts the error; actual adjoints are covered by the clean-subspace hybrid. Successful branches preserve the actual good ray, not an independent fresh preparation.
